note: A submission is scored relation by relation. It is not an overall accuracy score. The examples below use placeholders, not hidden labels.

operations.line: <int: 1-based source line of the downstream statement>
operations.text: <string: the source line, optional but recommended>

relations.input: <object: argument name -> value; must be in the declared legal domain>
relations.condition: <string: restricted boolean expression over argument names; see condition_language>
relations.explanation: <string: one sentence explaining why this operation set changes the masking relation>

counterexample.note: null, or an object with key input: a legal input where deleting A changes the observable
counterexample.input: <object: legal input where deleting A changes the observable>

guard.expr: <string: restricted boolean expression over argument names; true when A is masked>

test_gap.verdict: unexercised | masked | would_be_caught | assertion_gap | test_broken | not_covered

fields.evidence: <string: executable observations or source positions the method wants scored>

condition_language.forbidden: function calls, attribute access, names not in the argument list, string constants

semantics.independent: condition is true on inputs where the single declared operation, enabled alone, makes P+ and P- observationally equal
semantics.cooperative: condition is true on inputs where the declared operation set, enabled alone, makes P+ and P- observationally equal, and no proper non-empty subset does
semantics.coexisting: condition is true on inputs where disabling the declared operation set makes P+ and P- observationally different, and no proper non-empty subset of it does
